record.title: Proposed amendment to Board of Governors Regulation 1.001, University Board of Trustees Powers and Duties (disclosure of AI use in course syllabi)
record.short_title: Florida BOG Regulation 1.001 amendment: AI syllabus disclosure
record.issuing_body: Board of Governors of the State University System of Florida
record.summary: Proposed amendment to the Board of Governors regulation that sets the composition, organisation and powers of the boards of trustees of Florida's public universities. It would require each university board of trustees to establish policies requiring every course syllabus to disclose the faculty's use of artificial intelligence and the use of AI permitted to students. The same amendment would require boards of trustees to adopt policies maintaining institutional neutrality on contentious political and social issues.
record.notes: Board staff proposed the amendment for the Board meeting of 3 Sep 2026, where the Board was asked to approve a public notice of intent to amend the regulation. The day before, the Board's Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity Task Force was briefed on the proposed AI transparency language. If the Academic Affairs Committee and the Board approved the notice, the amended regulation would be open for public comment for 14 days and, if no concerns were raised, would return to the Board for final approval at its next meeting. The Board acts under Article IX, Section 7 of the Florida Constitution.
record.scope_note: Mainly an amendment on university trustees' powers and institutional neutrality whose AI part is a single transparency duty (disclosing AI use in course syllabi); included as the State University System's AI rule-making alongside the State Board of Education's AI rules.

verification.note: Stored the Board of Governors agenda item for the meeting of 3 Sep 2026, which describes the proposed amendment and the notice-and-comment procedure, and the agenda item of the Board's Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity Task Force of 2 Sep 2026 on the proposed AI transparency language (both flbog.edu). The amended regulation text, the outcome of the 3 Sep 2026 vote and any final approval are not in the stored sources; flbog.edu regulation pages refuse automated requests. flbog.edu is not yet listed in pipeline/official-sites.json, so the evidence counts as secondary until a human reviews the host.
